hook: Gates co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen in 1975 and has since become one of the most widely read public commentators on artificial intelligence's likely effects on work, health, and education. His 2023 essay declaring that the age of AI had begun was among the most widely circulated executive statements on the technology that year.

reading.body:
Bill Gates has become one of the most widely heard voices on AI's consequences for society, with his 2023 declaration that "the age of AI has begun" reaching a mass audience and his 2025 predictions about work restructuring extending that influence into mainstream media.

His commentary frames AI as comparable in historical significance to the microprocessor, personal computer, internet, and mobile phone. This positions AI not as a narrow technical capability but as a general-purpose transformation. Gates speaks about AI's effects on labor, health, and education rather than on the underlying systems that enable AI deployment. His public statements reach audiences beyond technology circles, shaping how non-technical audiences understand AI's timeline and scope.

The data does not cover the accuracy of his predictions, the extent to which his statements have influenced policy or investment, or his specific technical positions on compute scaling or power requirements. It establishes only that he holds a prominent platform and uses it to communicate about AI to the general public.

standing.watch: What remains unresolved in the records is the litigation. The New York Times case and the Authors Guild class action are both in discovery, both consolidated into MDL 1:25-md-03143, and the Times matter has summary judgment briefing closed as of April 2, 2026, with no outcome recorded here. Gates's own position is the other open thread: his late September 2026 statements that self-regulation is not enough and that mandatory government oversight is needed are calls, not settled policy, and the records show no response to them. The company entry for Microsoft carries no funding or valuation figures, and no planned listing or dispute naming Gates himself appears anywhere in these records. Where the records are thin, they stay thin: one company, two cases, and a run of commentary.
standing.record: The site's records on Gates add up to one company and two lawsuits. Microsoft, founded in 1975 in Redmond, Washington, is the only company listed, and it appears as a defendant in The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI, which is in discovery with summary judgment briefing closed on April 2, 2026, and in Authors Guild v. OpenAI, Inc., a class action in discovery. Both have been consolidated into MDL 1:25-md-03143, the Authors Guild matter before Judge Stein. Neither case names Gates personally. The 26 news stories that name him, the latest dated September 29, 2026, are almost entirely about his warnings that AI is powerful enough to cause a billion deaths if unchecked and his calls for legislation. The pattern is consistent: the litigation attaches to the company he co-founded, while the coverage attaches to him as a commentator and advocate.
standing.standing: Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen in 1975 and stepped down from Microsoft's board of directors on March 13, 2020, so he holds no board seat at the company the records tie to him. He is co-chair of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. His influence in artificial intelligence, as these records show it, runs through writing and public argument rather than through operating an AI business: his essay The Age of AI has begun, published on GatesNotes on March 21, 2023, was among the most widely circulated executive statements on the technology that year. In March 2025 he told The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon that AI could shrink the work week to two or three days. By late September 2026 he was joining calls for AI safeguards and saying that self-regulation is not enough, with coverage describing him as backing mandatory government oversight of AI safety. Microsoft remains the one company on this site connected to him, and it is a defendant in the AI copyright cases listed here.

timeline.event: Co-founds Microsoft with Paul Allen on April 4, 1975.
timeline.impact: Starts the company that becomes a dominant force in personal computing software.

timeline.event: Steps down from Microsoft's board of directors on March 13, 2020.
timeline.impact: Ends his formal governance role at the company, per Microsoft's own announcement.

timeline.event: Publishes The Age of AI has begun on GatesNotes on March 21, 2023.
timeline.impact: Argues that generative AI is as significant as the microprocessor, the PC, the internet, and the mobile phone.

timeline.event: Predicts on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon in March 2025 that AI could reduce the standard work week to two or three days within about a decade.
timeline.impact: Extends his public commentary on AI from technology to its effects on labor.
